description: Compiler eval cases. Each case is a natural-language request plus checkable structural expectations, not a gold graph, because many different graphs can be correct. Rules: requiredKinds (each kind appears at least once), requiredAnyOf (each group needs at least one of its kinds), forbiddenKinds (none may appear), mustPrecede [A, B] (every node of kind B has a node of kind A among its ancestors), parallel [A, B] (some node of kind A and a different node of kind B exist where neither is an ancestor of the other), minKindCount (kind -> minimum count), branchCount (exact number, or {min,max}, of branch nodes), nodeCount ({min,max} total nodes), triggerEvent (the trigger's event), acceptCompileError (for ambiguous/adversarial cases a clean CompileError also counts as a pass). RAG cases assume the seeded sample knowledge base (kb_sample_handbook) is indexed.

cases.prompt: When a webhook arrives, summarize the body with an LLM and post the summary to #updates in Slack.
Every morning at 9am, fetch https://api.example.com/metrics and post the raw numbers to #metrics.
When I click run, take the text I paste in, translate it to Spanish with an LLM, and give me back the translation.
When a GitHub webhook for a new issue arrives, have an LLM classify it as bug, feature or question and output JSON with the label.
Every Friday at 5pm, call our sales API at https://sales.example.com/weekly, have an LLM write a short weekly report from it, and post the report to #sales.
When a form submission webhook arrives, pull out the name and email fields and POST them to https://crm.example.com/contacts.
Whenever I run this manually, generate a promo badge image that says 'Launch Week'.
When a webhook with a customer review arrives, rate its sentiment from 1 to 5 using a fast, cheap model and send the score to https://reviews.example.com/scores.
On a webhook, lowercase the email field, trim whitespace from the name, and forward the cleaned payload to https://api.example.com/users.
Every hour, have an LLM write a short motivational quote and post it to #random.
When a support ticket webhook arrives, have an LLM classify its sentiment. If the sentiment is negative, alert #support in Slack, otherwise log it by POSTing to https://logs.example.com/tickets.
When a GitHub pull request webhook arrives, if the PR was merged post 'Merged!' to #dev, otherwise do nothing.
On a payment webhook, if the amount is over 1000 post it to #finance; otherwise post it to #payments.

When an order webhook comes in, check the country field. If it's the US, send the order to https://us.example.com/orders. If it's an EU country, send it to https://eu.example.com/orders. Anything else goes to #intl-orders on Slack.
Every 15 minutes fetch https://api.example.com/health. If the response says the status is down, have an LLM write a short incident summary and post it to #incidents.
When a new signup webhook arrives, use an LLM to decide whether the email looks like spam. If it's spam, drop it. If not, post a welcome message to #new-users.

When a deploy webhook arrives and the deploy failed: if the environment is production, page the on-call engineer by POSTing to https://pager.example.com/alert; if it's staging, just post a note to #staging.
On a webhook carrying an invoice, have an LLM extract the total as JSON, then if the total is above 5000 send it to #approvals, otherwise send it to https://erp.example.com/invoices.

Every morning, fetch the weather from https://weather.example.com/today and the news from https://news.example.com/top in parallel, then have an LLM combine them into one message and post it to #morning.
When a new blog post webhook arrives, in parallel have one LLM write a tweet, another write a LinkedIn post, and a third write a newsletter blurb. Then combine all three and post them to #marketing.

When a lead webhook arrives, simultaneously enrich it from https://enrich.example.com/person and look up the company at https://companies.example.com/lookup, then merge both results and POST the combined lead to https://crm.example.com/leads.
When I run this manually, generate a banner image and a badge image at the same time, then post both to #design.

When a support question comes in by webhook, search the employee handbook knowledge base and, in parallel, fetch the customer's account from https://api.example.com/accounts. Then have an LLM answer using both and post the answer to #support.

Every Monday, fetch open issues from https://api.github.com/repos/acme/app/issues and open pull requests from https://api.github.com/repos/acme/app/pulls at the same time, summarize both with one LLM, and post the summary to #eng.
When a refund request webhook arrives, have an LLM draft a reply email, but ask me to approve it before sending it via POST to https://mail.example.com/send.
Every day, draft a social media post with an LLM and wait for my approval before posting it to #social.
When an expense webhook arrives, if the amount is over 500 require manager approval before forwarding it to https://finance.example.com/pay; smaller amounts are forwarded immediately.

When a contract link arrives by webhook, have an LLM summarize the key terms, post the summary to #legal, and pause for legal's approval. Once approved, POST the contract to https://docs.example.com/sign.
Every night at 2am, run the database cleanup by calling https://db.example.com/cleanup, but have a human approve it first.
When a webhook with a list of orders arrives, for each order compute the total including 20% tax, then post the list of totals to #orders.
Every hour, fetch the list of open tickets from https://helpdesk.example.com/tickets, keep just the id and title of each ticket, and post that list to #helpdesk.
For each item in the incoming webhook's list of product IDs, call the API at https://shop.example.com/products.
When a webhook with a list of customer feedback strings arrives, clean up each string by trimming and lowercasing it, then have an LLM summarize the main themes and post them to #product.
When a question arrives by webhook, answer it from the HR policy knowledge base and reply in Slack in #hr-help.
When an employee question comes in by webhook, look up the answer in the employee handbook and return an answer with citations.
When someone asks about expense limits via webhook, search the handbook and answer with an LLM. If the answer says manager approval is needed, post it to #finance-questions; otherwise just return it.
Every Monday morning, pull the remote work policy from the knowledge base and have an LLM write a 3-bullet reminder for #general.
do the thing with my emails
When a Shopify order comes in, add the customer to Salesforce and print a shipping label on the office printer.
